title: improv·artist · improvisational (Jackson Pollock)
mutation_directive: improv artist: improvisational via Jackson Pollock

improv_extras.practice: all-over drip; whole-body rhythm; controlled chaos; no center

v1.feedback: The Pollock concept lands — multiple swing streams with figure-eight pivots and tangential drip arcs produce genuine all-over composition rather than a centered blob, and the gestural burst mechanic adds convincing fling energy. The Aizawa attractor vestige feels like dead weight though; it's flattened to near-zero z influence and the swing forces dominate, so it reads as inherited code rather than a deliberate design choice — strip it or let it visibly shape the skeins. The palette cycling through warm earth tones is appropriate but the additive blending washes out to near-white in dense regions, losing the layered-enamel quality of actual Pollock drip paintings; try a darker multiply or screen blend with opacity falloff so you can read individual skeins overlapping. Camera is static and framing is decent but slightly too much empty margin at the edges — tighten the view or let respawn bounds match the visible frame so paint fills the canvas edge-to-edge as Pollock's work does.

v2.feedback: The lemniscate swing-arm metaphor is a genuine Pollock encoding, and the top-down ortho camera correctly frames the floor-canvas — but the elastic pull toward 9 distinct figure-eight paths will read as an organized spirograph, not Pollock's tangled all-over field. The brief says 'no center,' yet the radial pivot layout creates an obvious center. To fix: drop the per-skein elastic tether and instead accumulate particle trails into a persistent FBO (paint layer) — Pollock's power is in the dried trace, not the live particle; add 3–5 layered passes at different speeds/scales so skeins cross and occlude each other, breaking individual curve readability. The Aizawa attractor feels bolted on for turbulence when physical variance (random wrist-snap timing, variable pour height) would be more conceptually honest.
